evidence.snippet: if you are using the API for yourself as a Direct Developer, you do not need Advanced access or app review.
If you are building an app that other businesses will be using, you must request Advanced access for any permissions your app needs.
before you can use your app in a production capacity, you must create your own endpoint.

decisions.reason: Pages show self-serve build/test is possible but production use for partners/multi-customer apps requires Advanced access via App Review, matching the app_review definition exactly.

evidence.snippet: WhatsApp account management: Create accounts, add and remove phone numbers, link accounts together, and assign partner access.
Webhooks Webhooks deliver JSON payloads to your server for message status updates, incoming messages, asynchronous error handling,

decisions.reason: Both agents agree and pages show many resource types (accounts, templates, webhooks, analytics, numbers) consistent with a broad API surface.

evidence.snippet: Bearer token for API authentication. This should be a valid access token obtained through the appropriate OAuth flow or system user token.
Authentication uses OAuth (not 2.0) access tokens, while permissions restrict access to specific resources.
System user access tokens ("system tokens") represent you, your business, organization, or people within your business or organization.

decisions.reason: API calls are authenticated via long-lived system-user tokens sent as Bearer tokens, while onboarding (Embedded Signup/Facebook Login) uses an OAuth-style flow, so both methods are supported per the pages.
